transcript.text: Hello, I'm here to help you get ready for your appointment. Could you tell me what has been bothering you?
It's my right knee, mainly. The pain has been getting worse and it's really starting to hold me back.
When did you first notice it?
It only started getting bad last week.
Is there anything that makes it better or worse?
Going down stairs is the worst, and it starts aching after I've been walking for more than about ten minutes. It eases off if I sit down and take some paracetamol.
How would you describe the feeling in your own words?
It's a deep, grinding sort of ache. And the knee feels stiff in the morning for about twenty minutes before it loosens up.
Where exactly do you feel it, and does it spread anywhere?
It's on the inner side of the right knee. It doesn't spread down the leg or anything like that.
On a scale from 0 to 10, where 10 is the worst, how bad is it?
On a bad day it's about a 7 out of 10. I can't even walk the dog round the park anymore like I used to.
Is it there all the time, or does it come and go?
It comes and goes — it's not there every minute. It's worse after I've been on my feet, and it settles when I rest.
Has anything else been bothering you along with this?
The knee sometimes swells up a bit by the evening. But there's no redness, and I haven't had any fever or the knee locking up.
Do you see a doctor regularly for any health condition?
Yes, I've got type 2 diabetes — had it about ten years now. And I had a stent put in a heart artery about six years ago.
Which medicines do you take regularly, including any new ones?
I take metformin, 1 gram twice a day. And aspirin 75 mg once a day, atorvastatin 40 mg at night, and ramipril 5 mg once a day.
Are you allergic to any medicines?
Penicillin gives me a rash, so I have to avoid that.
Has this changed what you can do around the house or outside?
Yes — going downstairs I have to take it one step at a time and hold the rail now. I can't manage the dog walk round the park anymore either.
Is there anything about this that worries you?
I'd like something stronger for the pain, to be honest. And I've been wondering — do you think I might end up needing a knee replacement?
Thank you, that is very helpful. I have put together a short summary of what you told me. Please read it and tell me if anything should be corrected before it goes to your doctor.
